To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the current vector control tools are not sufficient to control malaria and that new eco friendly tools are urgently needed to reduce or eliminate the burden of malaria.
the current vector control methods are not sufficient to reduce malaria incidence and that novel eco friendly control strategies should be tested and developed in the near future.

the development and evaluation of new mosquito control strategies require a trans-disciplinary cooperation among parasitology, entomology and ecology, and that the optimization of processes and tools for mosquito control delivery is crucial to improve the effectiveness of current vector control programs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new eco friendly tools to fight malaria and other mosquito transmitted diseases.
the development and evaluation of innovative vector control tools and strategies to control malaria and other vector borne diseases.
the development of novel and eco friendly tools that will reduce the burden of malaria in Africa.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the fight against malaria is not over and that the current vector control strategies are not sufficient to reach the Millennium Development Goals (MDGs) for malaria elimination.
there is a need for new vector control strategies to be developed to reduce the burden of mosquito borne diseases, especially in Africa.
current vector control challenges are still a major problem and that the fight against malaria will continue.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the fight against malaria is far from over, despite the recent progress in the fight against the disease.
we have demonstrated that the use of a novel mosquito repellent (NMP) in combination with a novel mosquito trap (NTT) is a promising approach to control the malaria vectors.
the current strategies for malaria management are not sufficient to eliminate this disease from Africa and that novel technologies are needed to control outdoor transmission.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a better understanding of the behavioral ecology of malaria mosquitoes is required to develop effective and eco friendly vector control strategies.
the development of novel vector control strategies should be based on the understanding and the careful evaluation of the epidemiologic impact triggered by novel tools.
the fight against malaria requires a trans disciplinary approach.
